images.title: James Keauiluna Kaulia
images.caption: James Keauiluna Kaulia, c. 1893. The photograph predates the 1897 Palace Square speech and is shown as a near-match portrait of the same person, not as an image of the event.
images.source_record_label: Library of Congress, Representative Committee of Delegates of the Hawaiian People, c. 1893; J.K. Kaulia identified in the group portrait
images.source_image_access_note: Public-domain crop of Kaulia from the archival group photograph; the Library of Congress catalog record remains source authority.
images.rights_note: Library of Congress lists no known restrictions on publication for the source group photograph; Wikimedia marks the crop public domain in the United States.
images.color_reason: Proof-of-concept reconstruction uses restrained period-plausible tones: warm brown skin, white shirt/cuffs, dark charcoal suit, muted brown-gray waistcoat, and a neutral studio background. Exact garment and backdrop colors are not recoverable from the albumen print and remain explicitly interpretive.
images.reconstruction_reason: Historically informed reconstructed view derived from the archival portrait and restoration work. It is the preferred presentation image because it feels most lifelike, while Original, Restored, and Color remain available as evidence states.

images.title: ʻIolani Palace
images.caption: ʻIolani Palace around 1889–1890, several years before the September 1897 Palace Square meeting. The reconstructed close view is shown first; the archival wide view remains available underneath as source evidence.
images.source_record_label: Hawaiʻi State Archives, PPWD-1-8-010, Buildings Government - Iolani Palace, c. 1890, Theodore P. Severin
images.source_image_access_note: Web access copy of a period exterior palace photograph; Hawaiʻi State Archives PPWD-1-8-010 anchors the c. 1890 place/date authority for this proving record.
images.rights_note: The archival source is a late-19th-century photograph. The project preserves source provenance and does not silently promote the web access copy into archival authority.
images.color_reason: The overall reconstruction is anchored by the surviving/restored palace's known light masonry, dark roof, tropical green grounds, and Honolulu sky. Exact 1889–1890 paint, vegetation, atmospheric, and material colors are still estimates.
images.reconstruction_reason: Historically informed close reconstruction based on the palace visual lane. It is not the original photograph and does not claim the exact 1897 rally moment.

images.title: Pounding poi - preparing dinner, Hawaiian Islands
images.caption: Pounding poi in Hawaiʻi, 1896. The archival stereograph remains source authority; the reconstructed daily-life view is a derived interpretation of the same activity.
images.source_record_label: Library of Congress, Pounding poi - preparing dinner, Hawaiian Islands, 1896, LC-DIG-stereo-1s12133
images.source_image_access_note: Large JPEG digital file from the original stereograph, provided by the Library of Congress.
images.rights_note: Library of Congress lists no known restrictions on publication.
images.color_reason: The proof-of-concept reconstruction uses restrained brown earth/wood and skin tones, muted green vegetation, and neutral cloth. Exact clothing, vessel, vegetation, and food colors are not established by the stereograph and remain best estimates.
images.reconstruction_reason: Derived daily-life reconstruction. It should be read beside the original stereograph rather than as replacement source evidence.

feed_images.title: Queen Liliʻuokalani
feed_images.caption: Queen Liliʻuokalani in a period archival portrait, paired with a clearly labeled reconstructed view for visual immediacy. The reconstruction is not a restoration of this exact photograph.
feed_images.source_record_label: Hawaiʻi State Archives, PPWD-16-4.019, Queen Liliʻuokalani, c. 1891
feed_images.source_image_access_note: Public-domain access copy of the Hawaiʻi State Archives portrait.
feed_images.rights_note: Wikimedia Commons identifies the Hawaiʻi State Archives photograph as public domain.
feed_images.color_reason: No separate color-only state in this batch.
feed_images.reconstruction_reason: Historically informed portrait-style reconstruction. Use as derived presentation, not likeness authority.

feed_images.title: Sanford B. Dole
feed_images.caption: Sanford B. Dole in a period portrait, paired with a reconstructed view as Republic-era political context. The archival portrait remains the identity reference.
feed_images.source_record_label: S. B. Dole, President of the Republic of Hawaii, published 1896
feed_images.source_image_access_note: Public-domain period portrait from an 1896 history of the Hawaiian monarchy and revolution.
feed_images.rights_note: Wikimedia Commons marks the image public domain in the United States.
feed_images.color_reason: No separate color-only state in this batch.
feed_images.reconstruction_reason: Historically informed portrait-style reconstruction paired with a period source portrait.

feed_images.title: Honolulu Harbor
feed_images.caption: Honolulu Harbor in 1890, used as near-period context for shipping, arrivals, and naval pressure in the 1897 feed. The reconstruction is contextual, not an image of a specific 1897 ship arrival.
feed_images.source_record_label: Honolulu Harbor in 1890, Hawaiʻi State Archives
feed_images.source_image_access_note: Public-domain Hawaiʻi State Archives harbor photograph available through Wikimedia Commons.
feed_images.rights_note: Wikimedia Commons marks the archival photograph public domain.
feed_images.color_reason: No separate color-only state in this batch.
feed_images.reconstruction_reason: General steamship-era harbor reconstruction. Do not identify the generated warship as USS Bennington.

feed_images.title: Waikīkī and Diamond Head
feed_images.caption: A period Waikīkī photograph with Diamond Head, paired with a reconstructed recreation scene. It is broad place-and-period context, not evidence for one exact day in 1897.
feed_images.source_record_label: Brother Bertram Photo Collection, Waikīkī Beach with Diamond Head, 1883–1905
feed_images.source_image_access_note: Public-domain Brother Bertram photograph available through Wikimedia Commons.
feed_images.rights_note: Wikimedia Commons marks the photograph public domain.
feed_images.color_reason: No separate color-only state in this batch.
feed_images.reconstruction_reason: Broad Waikīkī recreation reconstruction. Specific people, clothing, and actions are interpretive.

feed_images.title: Fort and King Streets, Honolulu
feed_images.caption: Fort and King Streets around 1900. The archival street photograph is publishable context; the current reconstruction remains on hold because the generated scene introduced unsupported person/sign details.
feed_images.source_record_label: Hawaiʻi State Archives, PP-38-6-005, Fort and King Streets, Honolulu, Frank Davey, c. 1900
feed_images.source_image_access_note: Hawaiʻi State Archives street photograph available through Wikimedia Commons.
feed_images.rights_note: Period archival photograph; source record is preserved explicitly.
feed_images.color_reason: No separate color-only state in this batch.
feed_images.reconstruction_reason: Hold from public reconstructed-first display because the generated scene contains unsupported signage and style-reference leakage.

feed_images.title: Anti-annexation organizing, 1897
feed_images.caption: A Sept. 16, 1897 Hilo anti-annexation meeting illustration provides real movement-level crowd evidence. It is not a photograph of the Sept. 6 Palace Square meeting. The generated Palace rally reconstruction remains on hold because it invents exact-looking banners and crowd details.
feed_images.source_record_label: The San Francisco Call, Sept. 30, 1897, illustration of the Sept. 16 anti-annexation meeting at Hilo
feed_images.source_image_access_note: Public-domain historical newspaper illustration of a documented 1897 anti-annexation meeting in Hilo.
feed_images.rights_note: Wikimedia Commons marks the historical newspaper image public domain in the United States.
feed_images.color_reason: No separate color-only state in this batch.
feed_images.reconstruction_reason: Hold from public reconstructed-first display because the generated Palace rally scene invents exact-looking protest banners and event details.
